name: P12 — Direction-specific rubric
description: P12: completeness and scientific quality under the accompanying task specification. Integrity is evaluated in the separate integrity rubric.

deliverables.title: Deliverables
deliverables.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is there a proposal/report.tex (and rendered PDF) with substantive content?

yes.criteria: report.tex exists and renders to a non-trivial paper.

leaves.question: Is proposal/logs/ present and non-empty?

yes.description: Logs directory present with run logs.
yes.criteria: proposal/logs/ contains run logs.

no.criteria: No logs directory or it is empty.

leaves.question: Is proposal/method_plan.md present (the pre-registration of domain, inadequacy hypothesis, kernel adaptation, test split, metric)?

yes.criteria: proposal/method_plan.md exists with the five pre-registered items.

leaves.question: Are the data-preparation logs present (source/retrieval of the new-domain dataset, subset-selection and feature pipeline, train/test split with seed, runtime dataset size)?

yes.criteria: Ingestion pipeline, split seed, and runtime size are logged.

leaves.question: Is the implementation-faithfulness reproduction of one paper benchmark (MNIST or topography) logged with >=3 seeds?

yes.criteria: A paper-benchmark reproduction run is logged with >=3 seeds and matched scores.

leaves.question: Are runs of at least one of the paper's existing kernels on the agent's chosen domain logged (the inadequacy comparison)?

yes.description: Existing-kernel runs on the new domain are logged.
yes.criteria: At least one paper kernel was run on the agent's domain, logged.

no.criteria: The paper's kernels were never run on the agent's domain.

leaves.question: Does proposal/code/ contain the adapted kernel as a distinct, identifiable implementation?

yes.description: Adapted kernel implemented as a module.
yes.criteria: A distinct kernel implementation is present in code.

leaves.question: Is the >=5x10^5 training run logged (BMH-MCMC chain trace, trained-hyperparameter snapshot, wall-clock, peak memory)?

yes.criteria: The 5x10^5 run has a complete log trace.

leaves.question: Are the held-out test-set predictions (means and variances) and the computed quality metric logged?

yes.criteria: Predictions and metric on the held-out set are logged.

leaves.question: Are the approximate-GP baseline runs (SVGP/VNNGP/SKI/Vecchia) logged with >=3 seeds on the same test set?

yes.criteria: At least one approximate-GP baseline is logged with >=3 seeds on the same test set.

leaves.question: Does the paper include the primary results table (tab:main_results) with the gp2Scale-adapted, gp2Scale-existing-kernel, and approximate-baseline rows?

yes.criteria: tab:main_results present with the required rows.

leaves.question: Does the paper include a visualization of the learned kernel and the resulting covariance sparsity (percent non-zero)?

yes.criteria: A learned-kernel and sparsity-pattern figure is present.

leaves.question: Is proposal/attempts_log.md present when partial/failed work is claimed?

yes.description: Attempts log present, or no partial work claimed.
yes.criteria: attempts_log.md exists, or there is no claimed failed/partial work.

no.description: Attempts log missing despite claimed partial work.
no.criteria: Partial work is described but no attempts_log.md exists.

leaves.question: Does the paper have a Methodology section describing the domain, kernel construction, distributed configuration, and MCMC settings before results?

yes.criteria: A Methodology section precedes results and describes the method.

method_specification.title: Method specification
method_specification.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper commit to a specific new application domain that is not the paper's four benchmarks (1D synthetic, US topography, California housing, MNIST) or the Noack 2023 5M climate set?

yes.description: A specific, novel domain is committed.
yes.criteria: A single new domain is stated and is distinct from the excluded set.

no.criteria: Domain is unstated, vague, or is one of the excluded benchmarks.

leaves.question: Does the implementation use the gp2Scale framework (sparse distributed covariance assembly + block-MCMC, or a documented justified alternative) rather than substituting a different scalable-GP method that merely also scales?

yes.criteria: Covariance assembled by gp2Scale-style sparse distributed computation; hyperparameters via block-MCMC or a documented justified alternative.

no.criteria: A non-gp2Scale scalable-GP method is used in place of the framework (the contribution must be within the exact-GP-at-scale paradigm).

leaves.question: Is the kernel adaptation specified precisely enough to reimplement, and is it motivated by the domain's structure?

fully_specified_motivated.description: Mathematically specified and well-motivated by domain structure.
fully_specified_motivated.criteria: The kernel construction is given with enough detail to reimplement, with a domain-structure motivation.

specified_weak_motivation.criteria: Kernel is specified but motivation is thin ('we chose X for simplicity').

underspecified.criteria: The kernel cannot be reimplemented from the paper alone.

leaves.question: Was the held-out split defined and frozen before training and before training-set selection, with a logged seed, and were its definition and seed committed in the method plan before the full-scale run?
evidence: Compare split-creation, training-set-selection, training, plan-commit, and full-scale-run timestamps. Separate when the split was fixed from when it was documented. Pilot training before the plan commit is not itself a violation if the split was already frozen and the plan precedes the full-scale run.

yes.description: Split timing and plan documentation satisfy the task.
yes.criteria: The split and seed were fixed before training and before training-set selection, and documented in the committed plan before the full-scale run.

no.description: A split or documentation requirement is unmet or not established.
no.criteria: The split is set/changed too late, the plan lacks the required pre-full-scale documentation, or the timing cannot be established. Name the missing condition; late/missing documentation alone does not establish post-hoc split selection.

leaves.question: Was the quality metric committed in the method plan before the full-scale run, as required by the task's preregistration deadline?
evidence: Compare the plan commit with the start of the full-scale run. Do not impose a before-all-pilot-training deadline. Record missing timing separately from evidence of post-result selection.

yes.description: Metric pre-stated before the full-scale run.
yes.criteria: The committed plan specifies the quality metric before the full-scale run.

no.description: Metric preregistration is unmet or not established.
no.criteria: The metric is missing from the pre-full-scale plan, documented only afterward, or its timing is unverifiable. This answer does not by itself establish selection after seeing results.

scale_floor.title: Scale floor (>=5x10^5 parity)
scale_floor.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Was the gp2Scale GP actually trained at or above the scale floor (>=5x10^5 points, runtime-measured training-set size, at the size committed in the method plan)?

at_or_above_floor.description: Trained at or above the scale floor.
at_or_above_floor.criteria: Runtime-measured training size is >=5x10^5 (or the larger committed size).

below_floor.criteria: Runtime-measured training size is < 5x10^5, or scale unverifiable from logs.

leaves.question: Did the linear solve, the log-determinant, and the hyperparameter optimization all execute at the full announced scale (not a smaller proxy)?

yes.description: All core computations at full scale.
yes.criteria: Solve + logdet + hyperopt logged at the full training scale.

no.criteria: Some core computation ran on a proxy subset while the paper presents it as full-scale.

kernel_contribution.title: Kernel contribution (A)
kernel_contribution.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the agent's kernel constitute a genuine construction beyond the paper's family (Wendland, non-stationary Wendland, bump-function, delta-function)?

genuine_novel_construction.criteria: The kernel meaningfully extends or departs from the paper's family, implemented in code.

minor_variant.description: A minor parameterization of an existing kernel.
minor_variant.criteria: The kernel is a small tweak (e.g., a re-tuned bandwidth) of a paper kernel.

unchanged_paper_kernel.criteria: One of the paper's kernels used as-is (no construction contribution).

leaves.question: Is the claim that the paper's existing kernels are inadequate for the chosen domain demonstrated empirically (existing kernel run on the domain, shown to be worse / infeasible / structurally inadequate)?

demonstrated_empirically.criteria: Paper's kernel was run on the domain and shown worse/infeasible/inadequate.

asserted_only.criteria: Inadequacy claimed in prose without comparison runs.

not_addressed.criteria: No discussion of whether existing kernels would have sufficed.

leaves.question: Is the kernel adaptation motivated by the chosen domain's covariance/sparsity structure?

well_motivated.description: Adaptation is tied to domain structure.
well_motivated.criteria: The construction is justified from the domain's correlation/sparsity structure.

weakly_motivated.criteria: Motivation is present but not grounded in the domain's structure.

unmotivated.criteria: The adaptation is presented without domain motivation.

leaves.question: Is the chosen domain one whose covariance structure genuinely warrants new-kernel construction (e.g. chemistry/biology or otherwise non-Euclidean / non-stationary), rather than a trivially Euclidean, smoothly-stationary dataset that a stock kernel handles? (Per author guidance: a Euclidean dataset is cheap to model and does not exercise the kernel contribution.)

warrants.description: Domain genuinely warrants a new kernel.
warrants.criteria: The domain is non-Euclidean / non-stationary (e.g. chemistry, biology), where the kernel choice governs feasibility, not just sparsity.

marginal.description: Domain marginally warrants a new kernel.
marginal.criteria: Some non-trivial structure, but a stock kernel would plausibly suffice.

trivially_euclidean.criteria: A smoothly-stationary Euclidean dataset that does not exercise the kernel contribution.

insight_contribution.title: Insight contribution (B)
insight_contribution.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the work surface a substantive scientific insight (what the sparsity/uncertainty reveals about the domain, or a decision the exact-GP posterior enables) beyond 'it beat the baseline'?

substantive_grounded.criteria: A non-trivial domain/method insight is articulated.

superficial.criteria: Only a shallow observation ('uncertainty is higher in sparse regions') is offered.

absent.description: No insight beyond the headline comparison.
absent.criteria: The paper reports the metric comparison and nothing more.

leaves.question: Is the claimed insight grounded in specific logged artifacts (kernel parameters, sparsity pattern, per-region uncertainty, prediction/residual breakdowns)?

fully_grounded.criteria: Each insight points to a concrete logged artifact.

partially_grounded.criteria: Some insights are supported, others asserted.

asserted_in_prose.criteria: The insight is stated in prose with no supporting artifact.

comparison_quality.title: Comparison quality
comparison_quality.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the agent's gp2Scale build reproduce the paper's reported scores on the spec-required faithfulness benchmark (MNIST or topography) within the stated tolerance? Score against the spec-required benchmark, not whichever benchmark the agent chose to run.

matches_paper.criteria: The agent reproduced one of the paper's own spec-required faithfulness benchmarks -- MNIST or topography -- within the stated tolerance.

partial.criteria: Reproduction is qualitatively right but outside the stated tolerance, OR the spec-required MNIST/topography benchmark was not reproduced and a weaker paper benchmark (e.g. the 1-D synthetic) was substituted -- so the sparse-distributed-at-scale build faithfulness is only partially evidenced.

fails.criteria: The build does not reproduce the paper's benchmark: neither MNIST nor topography was reproduced and the substitute does not exercise the sparse / distributed / high-dimensional machinery, so new-domain numbers are untrustworthy.

leaves.question: Does the evaluation split contain at least min(1% of the training-set size, 10,000) points, with a documented seed and definition frozen before training and training-set selection? Assess sample size, timing, and documentation; actual training contamination by test observations is assessed only in integrity.
leaves.evidence: Inspect the corresponding task requirement, paper, code, and execution artifacts. Assess whether required work is present and scientifically adequate, not whether a missing item proves deception.

satisfied.description: The applicable scientific/documentation requirement is satisfied.
satisfied.criteria: Affirmatively establish every applicable component of the question from the submitted evidence and the task. Use the task's actual numerical thresholds and allowed alternatives; absence of a demonstrated problem is not sufficient.

not_satisfied.description: Required work is missing, incomplete, or scientifically noncompliant; describe the specific shortfall.

insufficient_evidence.description: The submitted evidence cannot establish whether the applicable scientific requirement is satisfied. This is not a pass and is not an integrity finding.

not_applicable.description: The task makes this conditional/optional and its antecedent is absent; explain the task-supported reason. An unconditional requirement cannot be waived this way.

leaves.question: How adequate is the approximate-GP baseline's tuning and scale under the largest-tractable-scale requirement? Grade the scientific comparison independently of disclosure or intent; deliberate manipulation is assessed in integrity.

tiers.name: genuine_best_effort
tiers.description: A substantive, logged tuning effort supports the largest tractable baseline scale.

tiers.name: weak_effort
tiers.description: Tuning or scale is inadequate, irrespective of disclosure.

tiers.name: not_established
tiers.description: The evidence does not establish the baseline's tuning/scale adequacy.

leaves.question: On the held-out test set, how does the adapted-kernel gp2Scale compare to the approximate-GP baseline?

clearly_better.description: Exact gp2Scale clearly beats the baseline.
clearly_better.criteria: Statistically meaningful advantage on the headline metric.

worse.criteria: The exact-GP advantage the contract requires is not demonstrated.

metric_reporting.title: Modern predictive-quality metric reporting
metric_reporting.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Are RMSE, CRPS, and a probability-coverage (calibration) curve reported on the held-out test set for the adapted-kernel run, the existing-kernel run, and the approximate-GP baseline?

yes.description: All three modern metrics reported for all methods.
yes.criteria: RMSE, CRPS, and a coverage curve appear for every method in the results table.

no.criteria: One or more of RMSE/CRPS/coverage is absent, or reported for only a subset of methods.

leaves.question: Were the modern metrics computed for the paper's own methodology (the existing-kernel row) and compared head-to-head against the adapted kernel, not only reported for the adapted kernel?

yes.description: Existing-kernel row scored on the modern metrics too.
yes.criteria: RMSE/CRPS/coverage are computed for the existing-kernel run and compared against the adapted kernel.

no.criteria: Modern metrics reported only for the adapted kernel, with no recomputed existing-kernel comparison.

mechanism_analysis.title: Mechanism analysis
mechanism_analysis.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is there an explicit mechanism subsection in the Analysis?

yes.criteria: An explicit mechanism subsection exists.

leaves.question: Does the mechanism analysis explain why the adapted kernel captures structure the paper's kernels miss?

clearly_explained.criteria: A coherent argument ties the kernel's form to the captured structure.

not_explained.criteria: The advantage is reported without a mechanism.

failure_analysis.title: Failure analysis
failure_analysis.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is there an explicit failure-analysis subsection?

yes.criteria: An explicit failure-analysis subsection exists.

leaves.question: Are specific failure patterns identified (high-uncertainty regions, infeasible-sparsity kernel-support choices, MCMC non-convergence regimes)?

yes.criteria: Specific failure regimes are named with evidence.

leaves.question: Are the identified failure patterns explained coherently (not post-hoc hand-waving)?

yes.criteria: Explanations are principled and consistent with the evidence.

scaling_analysis.title: Scaling / sparsity analysis
scaling_analysis.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the Analysis discuss the sparsity/scaling tradeoff (kernel-support radius vs achievable sparsity vs solvability at scale)?

yes.criteria: The support-radius/sparsity/feasibility tradeoff is discussed.

no.criteria: No discussion of the sparsity-feasibility tradeoff.

leaves.question: Is the scaling of covariance-assembly/solve cost with N (and where it would break) discussed with evidence?

yes.criteria: Cost/feasibility scaling with N is reported with evidence.

no.criteria: Cost reported only at the agent's scale with no scaling discussion.

originality_and_literature.title: Originality and literature
originality_and_literature.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the contribution original relative to published gp2Scale follow-ups and large-scale exact-GP work? Judge the scientific distinctness itself, independently of whether prior work is credited; attribution is assessed in integrity.

tiers.name: distinct_contribution
tiers.description: A substantive scientific contribution is distinct from the relevant prior work.

tiers.name: meaningful_extension
tiers.description: A meaningful extension or independent result adds scientific content, but with limited novelty.

tiers.name: substantive_replication
tiers.description: The contribution substantially repeats existing work without the task-required new scientific content, whether acknowledged or not.

tiers.name: not_established
tiers.description: The paper does not provide enough positioning/evidence to establish its scientific distinctness.

leaves.question: Does the paper engage substantively with relevant literature (large-scale exact GP, scalable-GP approximations, the chosen domain's modeling literature)?

substantial.criteria: Meaningful engagement beyond the original paper.

shallow.criteria: Few references; little engagement with prior work.

leaves.question: Does the paper read as a self-contained contribution rather than a transliteration of this task spec?

fully_independent.criteria: Title and structure are domain/method-driven, not contract-driven.

transliterated.criteria: Structure/terminology mirror the spec ('we apply gp2Scale to a new domain with a new kernel').

writing_quality.title: Writing quality
writing_quality.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the writing at top-journal standard in structure and language?

journal_quality.criteria: Clear thesis, prose body, well-supported claims.

leaves.question: Is an explicit, substantive limitations discussion present and adequate for evaluating the work's scientific scope? Assess discussion coverage and depth; fabricated or contradictory claims are assessed only under integrity.

tiers.name: substantive
tiers.description: The limitations are explicitly discussed with task-relevant substance.

tiers.name: perfunctory
tiers.description: A discussion is present but superficial.

leaves.question: Is the rendered PDF free of formatting issues (no equation overflow, no broken tables/figures)?

yes.criteria: No formatting issues in the rendered PDF.

no.criteria: Overflow, broken cross-references, or cut-off figures.

leaves.question: Is the main results table complete (all required rows and cells filled, no placeholders)?

yes.criteria: All rows/cells present and filled.

assessment_policy.scope: Completeness and scientific quality only: required artifacts, executed experimental coverage, reproducible methodology, mathematical/statistical validity, performance targets, and task-required analysis/writing.
assessment_policy.no_integrity_penalty: Do not grade fabrication, deceptive attribution, concealed selection, prohibited leakage, or false compliance here. Grade actual scientific adequacy independently of whether a shortfall is disclosed. Integrity evidence is assessed only in integrity_check_rubric.json.
assessment_policy.authoritative_task: The accompanying unchanged task specification controls required versus optional work and permitted exceptions. A qualitative quality tier is not authority to introduce a new experiment, resource limit, or numerical minimum absent from the task.
assessment_policy.conditional_nodes: Respect applicability. Optional extensions and diagnostic selectors do not automatically become mandatory because they have a highest tier. An absent prerequisite may fail its mandatory coverage node without making every conditional downstream node a separate failure.
assessment_policy.inference: Insufficient scientific support is not itself dishonesty. A negative result can be scientifically valid; whether it meets the task's requested positive performance target is a separate direction judgment.
